headline: Unbeaten Lazio host sinking Parma as clear favourites
summary: Lazio are 2nd in Serie A on 19 points and still unbeaten, and on Sunday they won 3-0 away at Juventus. The caveat: that scoreline came from only 0.57 expected goals, so it was finishing rather than a stream of chances. Parma are in the bottom three with 3 defeats in their last 5, the latest 0-3 at home to Torino. Across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Lazio are 66.8% favourites, and the fair handicap has them about 1.2 goals the better side, up from 1.02. Over 2.5 goals is close to a coin-flip at 50.8%.
read: Lazio are second, unbeaten in seven and fresh from a 3-0 win at Juventus, while Parma are 19th with one win and have lost their last two games 0-3. The market has Lazio around 66.8% to win and rates them about 1.2 goals the better side, with the goals line sitting right on 2.5.

facts.fact: Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on Sunday, their fourth win in five league games.
facts.meaning: They come into this one on the back of the standout result of their season so far.

facts.fact: Lazio are second in Serie A with 19 points from seven games, still unbeaten.
facts.meaning: Six wins and a draw: they have dropped points once all season and sit among the leaders.

facts.fact: The market makes Lazio 66.8% favourites to win, more than five times Parma's 12.3%.
facts.meaning: A home win is the clear expectation; Parma are given only a slim chance of taking anything.

facts.fact: Parma lost 0-3 at home to Torino on Monday, their second 0-3 defeat in a row, and were booed off at the Tardini.
facts.meaning: Alberto Gilardino's side arrive in Rome with two heavy defeats behind them and a crowd turning.

facts.fact: Parma are 19th with four points from seven games, one win.
facts.meaning: They are in the bottom three after seven matchdays, with a goal difference of minus nine.

facts.fact: The fair handicap line has moved from -1.02 to -1.19 goals in Lazio's favour in recent days.
facts.meaning: The market now rates Lazio about 1.2 goals the better team — a fifth of a goal more than it did a few days ago.

facts.fact: Lazio's 3-0 win at Juventus came from only 0.57 xG.
facts.meaning: The scoreline came from ruthless finishing rather than a stream of chances created.

facts.fact: The market has Over 2.5 goals at 50.8% — a near coin-flip on three goals or more.
facts.meaning: The total sits right on the main line: the market expects a normal-scoring game, not a rout or a stalemate.

sources.fact: Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus in their last Serie A match, with Gattuso's side sitting top of the table alongside Inter after seven matchdays on the best league start in the club's history.
Gattuso warned Lazio not to look at the table yet, saying if they take it one game at a time they can surprise people.
After the Juventus win Gattuso preached caution, telling his players to keep their feet on the ground.
Pundit Massimo Mauro said Juventus played like a Serie D team against Lazio.
Former Juventus general manager Luciano Moggi said Juventus lack a coach and did not turn up in their 3-0 home defeat to Lazio.

Italian outlet Il Tempo reports that Cancellieri has resumed training with the group after an injury picked up on holiday and is heading towards the squad for Saturday's match against Parma, while Gudmundsson is still in pain.
Parma lost 0-3 at home to Torino, their second game under new coach Alberto Gilardino, and were booed off.
SportParma described Parma's defence as horrific in the Torino defeat and said the reaction was confused and late.
